video_title: With Trust Breaking The World Over, Quality Collateral Is Now Key | Jonathan Wellum
gist: Value manager Jonathan Wellum of Rocklinc lays out a '6 D's' macro framework (digitization/AI, debt, debasement, deglobalization, demographics, dear valuations) and argues that with global trust breaking down, hard-asset collateral—gold, silver, copper, uranium—and cheap, defensive quality businesses are the way to protect and compound capital while staying cautious on richly-priced AI names.

themes.theme: AI capex overshoot and market fragility

insights.claim: AI and AI-related stocks now make up roughly 45% of the S&P 500's market cap and over 70% of the NASDAQ 100's, so an AI correction would drag down far more of the broad market than most passive investors realize.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Even 'safe' index and non-tech ETF holders carry concentrated AI risk; check top holdings before assuming diversification.
insights.quote: AI and AI related stocks are like 45% of the S&P's market cap and 70 plus% of the NASDAQ 100's market cap.

insights.claim: A 'compute glut'—AI capacity racing ahead of demand and leaving idle 'dark compute' like the dark fiber of the dotcom bust—would likely trigger a 2008-style broad drawdown, not a contained 2000-style tech-only correction.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Position for contagion across energy, metals and financing sectors that fund AI buildout, not just tech, if compute demand disappoints.
insights.quote: I would suspect it would be more like 2008... it would affect the financial service sector which is financing a lot of this now increasingly.

insights.claim: Trillions in AI capex require hundreds of billions in eventual profit just to earn a 15% return on equity, and the returns, token pricing and data-center obsolescence are impossible to forecast—making premium AI valuations high-risk.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Demand a wide margin of safety on AI names; the burden of proof on profitability is enormous and unmet.
insights.quote: you pay a lot for a cheery consensus

insights.claim: Cheap, fast-improving Chinese AI models can handle 80-90% of enterprise tasks near-free, letting companies reserve costly frontier models for only the hardest 10%—commoditizing pricing and gutting the profit thesis of US AI leaders.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Watch for token-price commodification as a leading indicator of compressed US AI margins; a structural headwind US policy can't fix.
insights.quote: you've just ripped a lot of the profit guts out of the American ecosystem

insights.claim: Rather than owning pure-play AI, Rocklinc invests 'around' the theme via companies with only partial AI exposure—Brookfield assets on long-term contracts and Schneider Electric componentry—to get incremental lift without full valuation risk.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: A template for AI exposure with downside protection: buy diversified industrials with a growing but non-dominant AI segment.

insights.claim: The market's AI-driven sell-off of quality software companies was overstated: names like Roper Technologies fell from ~$500 to ~$300 on fears AI would replace vertical software, but customers keep buying for service, risk management and data, and shares rebounded to ~$400.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: AI-disruption fear creates buyable dislocations in sticky vertical-software franchises; look for embedded-workflow moats the market mispriced.

themes.theme: The 6 D's macro framework and portfolio posture

insights.claim: Wellum organizes investing around six secular 'D's—digitization/AI, debt, debasement, deglobalization, demographics, and dear (expensive) valuations—and hunts for defensive, well-priced businesses positioned within those trends.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: A durable lens for screening: favor companies riding these secular tailwinds while trading at rational valuations.

insights.claim: Rocklinc runs a concentrated 18-25 stock, buy-and-hold, Buffett/Munger-style book and currently holds about 20-23% cash as optionality to buy market weakness and dampen volatility.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: High cash plus concentration signals a defensive stance; the manager expects a buyable pullback and wants dry powder.
insights.quote: one of the best investment strategies is lethargy or sloth

insights.claim: US cash now yields over 4% while Canadian-dollar cash yields only ~2.5-3%, so holding cash as optionality carries far lower opportunity cost for USD-based investors.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: USD investors are paid to wait; the rate gap also underpins the debasement case for the loonie.

insights.claim: With global debt near 350% of GDP and US federal debt approaching $40 trillion (up from $30 trillion only a couple years ago), Wellum sees inflation/debasement as inevitable and a core reason to own inflation-proof monetary assets.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Structural debasement is the through-line justifying an overweight to hard monetary assets over fiat-denominated claims.
insights.quote: 350% debt to GDP around the world

themes.theme: Gold, silver and the collateral thesis

insights.claim: Central banks have accumulated so much gold that it now exceeds US Treasuries as a share of their reserve assets—evidence that nations no longer trust each other and are demanding hard collateral.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: The reserve-asset shift is a structural, price-insensitive bid for gold; treat it as a durable demand floor.
insights.quote: when you see all the central banks hoovering up the gold and this become a larger asset than the US treasuries in terms of their reserve assets... the world doesn't trust each other

insights.claim: Wellum believes the froth-clearing correction has built a solid base and precious metals have likely bottomed, with gold back near $4,500 (off a low just above $4,000) and silver recovering from the mid-$50s to mid-$60s (futures ~$6.66/... crossing $66).
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: The manager reads the reset as a re-entry setup, not a 2011/1980-style multi-year top; dollar-cost average rather than chase.

insights.claim: Rocklinc dollar-cost-averaged into miners during the early-year pullback, buying Agnico Eagle down from roughly C$330 to under C$200 at 'crazy cheap' cash-flow multiples for new client accounts.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence a disciplined value shop saw the metals dip as accumulation, not capitulation.

insights.claim: Structural supply deficits plus inelastic and growing demand for silver and copper give precious/industrial metals a unique price floor, making a prolonged 2011-style 'dead money' decade unlikely.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Supply-side scarcity, not just monetary demand, underpins the bull case—favor producers and streamers with reserves.

themes.theme: Deglobalization, reshoring and the Western Hemisphere

insights.claim: The post-1980s globalization wave is reversing into a Hamiltonian reshoring trade, with tariffs pressuring capital back to the US and Western Hemisphere—benefiting logistics/industrials like Prologis and Carlisle Companies (siding/roofing) tied to re-industrialization.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Own industrial/real-estate 'picks and shovels' of reshoring with strong installed bases getting incremental growth.

insights.claim: A 'Monroe Doctrine 2.0' integrating the Americas is nearly inevitable: the hemisphere holds every critical resource, has ocean protection, and can unlock trapped South American resources plus cheaper labor—reducing dependence on China and the volatile Middle East.
insights.speaker: Adam Taggart
insights.so_what: Position for hemispheric supply-chain and resource integration as a multi-year investment theme.

insights.claim: Canada is a 'bonanza of trapped resources'—100+ years of oil and gas beyond US reserves—and American capital is increasingly circling the Canadian oil and gas sector, which trades cheaply amid GDP-per-capita stagnation over 11 years.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Cheap Canadian energy names offer re-rating upside if policy loosens and US capital flows in.

insights.claim: Government mining summits are converging on both sides of the border—a White House mining conference and Mark Carney's mid-September Toronto mining summit—signaling political will to fast-track critical-mineral development even from left-leaning leaders.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Policy tailwinds are lining up behind domestic mining; watch permitting acceleration as a catalyst for developers.

themes.theme: Mining, copper and technology-driven cost cuts

insights.claim: Drone-mounted electron/geophysical remote sensing can map subsurface veins before drilling, cutting the huge cost of deep drilling and improving both cost-per-ounce and extraction yield—an emerging edge for exploration.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Cost-reducing exploration tech is a differentiator; favor developers deploying it to de-risk resource definition.

insights.claim: Copper faces a massive structural deficit requiring an estimated ~$250 billion of new mine investment over coming years, and mines take a decade to build—supporting a strong long-term copper price floor.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Underinvestment plus long lead times favor incumbent producers and streamers with existing copper exposure.

insights.claim: Energy is 25-30% of a mine's operating cost, so small/micro modular nuclear reactors that can run 10+ years in remote sites like Ontario's Ring of Fire would be transformative—lowering costs and speeding development of otherwise stranded deposits.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Micro-nuclear is a call option on unlocking remote mines; pairs with the uranium/AI-power demand thesis.

insights.claim: Deposits are yielding newly valuable byproducts like germanium that were never tested for before because they lacked industrial demand—now critical for the tech industry.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Existing polymetallic assets may hold hidden strategic-metal optionality as tech demand redefines what's economic.

themes.theme: Specific portfolio names and streamer/royalty edge

insights.claim: Wellum favors owning commodity-fund manager Sprott Inc. over its ~50 ETFs directly—capturing all the ETF revenue with more leverage—and views it as a likely takeover candidate within 3-5 years, if not sooner.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: The asset-manager captures fee flow on rising commodity AUM; frames it as both a leveraged play and an M&A target.
insights.quote: Why own the ETF when you can own the company that's going to receive all the revenues from the ETFs?

insights.claim: Rocklinc's precious-metals book spans royalty/streaming names (Gold Royalty/GROY, Osisko Royalties, Royal Gold, Wheaton Precious Metals, Franco-Nevada) plus miner Agnico Eagle and speculative Power Metallic—layering de-risked cash flow with optionality.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: A concrete watchlist mixing low-risk royalty compounders with higher-beta exploration for asymmetric upside.

insights.claim: Franco-Nevada's Cobre Panama copper mine is likely to be restarted soon on compelling economics, and streamers like Wheaton are doing large silver streams on copper mines (e.g., with BHP)—expanding streaming into base metals.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: A Cobre Panama restart is a specific catalyst for Franco-Nevada; base-metal streaming widens streamers' opportunity set.

insights.claim: Insurance is an overlooked value pocket: commercial P&C insurers with combined ratios of 60-70 (30% underwriting margins) and large investment portfolios can grow earnings double-digits even at 2-3% top-line growth, yet trade at 8-9x earnings—a fraction of the market multiple.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Buy low-multiple P&C insurers in the soft part of the cycle; book-value compounding plus a cycle turn drives outsized returns.

insights.claim: Junior explorer Honeybadger (run by Chad Williams, backed by Rick Rule and Eric Sprott) is cheap after a four-month lock-up unwind: shares raised at 16 cents now trade ~70-80 cents and sold off on profit-taking, with fully-permitted Prairie Creek silver assets giving high-upside/low-downside optionality.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: A specific speculative name where a mechanical post-financing sell-off may offer entry below insider accumulation prices.

insights.claim: Wellum frames speculative mining entry with an 'elevator' rule: you don't need to buy on floor one—getting on at floor 10 after early check-marks are met still captures most of a 100-floor ride with far less risk.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Prioritize de-risking milestones over earliest entry; a discipline for sizing speculative resource positions.
insights.quote: you don't have to get on... on floor one. You can get on floor 10 and you still got a fantastic ride.

themes.theme: AI upside in productivity, health and government

insights.claim: AI's clearest near-term value is in pattern-recognition-heavy fields—medical diagnostics/imaging, drug discovery (e.g., Royalty Pharma using AI), fraud/waste auditing of government budgets, and cybersecurity—that can lower costs and offset demographic labor shortages.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: The durable AI winners may be application/vertical plays in health, security and audit rather than the capex-heavy infrastructure layer.

insights.claim: Aging demographics across most of the world (few countries with high fertility) plus heavy debt mean productivity gains from AI, robotics and digitization are now necessary just to keep GDP from collapsing.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Demographic decline turns automation from optional to mandatory—structural demand support for productivity-tech providers.

insights.claim: Government fraud/waste won't be fixed by AI's capability alone—the binding constraint is political will, since much wasteful spending flows deliberately to favored constituencies.
insights.speaker: Jonathan Wellum
insights.so_what: Don't underwrite fiscal savings from AI-driven audits; the human/political factor caps the benefit.
